what_if.case: A check says 'Every trading day's cash is counted' fails with 'Not counted: 2026-09-14'
what_if.do: Count that day's drawer on End of Day (or close the drawer on the till), then come back and reload.

what_if.case: A mistake is found in a locked month
what_if.do: Do not reopen for small things: reverse or correct it in the current open month (Journals → Reverse, dated today). Only the owner reopens, with a reason, and only the latest locked month.

what_if.case: The payroll check warns
what_if.do: Approve the month's payroll on Payroll before locking, or it can never be posted into that month.

what_if.do: Press Customer, type the number, Find, Put them on the order. Their points are earned when paid; their rewards are offered when you take payment.

screens.title: Point of Sale — selling without internet

who.branch_manager: As the owner.

who.barista: As the cashier. Not: As the cashier.

what_if.case: The internet goes down at lunch
what_if.do: Keep selling quick sales by cash or card. Do not add discounts or customers. Do not close the browser's data. Sales go up by themselves when it is back.

what_if.case: A sale shows red after the internet came back
what_if.do: Ask a manager: Send again, Record at today's price, or (last) Take it off this till.

what_if.case: The batch came out lighter than the recipe says
what_if.do: Type what you weighed in 'What came out (optional)' with its unit. The preview shows '— {diff} less than the recipe's {planned}'. Record it: stock gets what really came out, at the full cost of the ingredients.

what_if.case: I made it this morning before opening and forgot to record it
what_if.do: A manager ticks 'Made earlier: yesterday or today, recorded now', gives the time and why, and records it. Not possible if a count of its items was approved after that time, or before yesterday.

what_if.case: An ingredient shows 'only … in stock'
what_if.do: Usually a delivery is not entered. Enter it on Purchasing first. If the item's rule allows it, a manager can approve using more with their PIN; if it refuses, record the delivery or count it first.

what_if.case: A batch was recorded twice by mistake
what_if.do: A manager presses 'Cancel…' on the second one in Batches, types 'recorded twice', and 'Cancel the batch'. If some of it was already sold or used, record the rest as a loss on Inventory instead.

what_if.case: A batch went soft and must be sold today
what_if.do: A manager uses 'Change the use-by…' in In stock by batch, gives today's time and the reason. It then appears under 'Sell it before it goes', where it can be marked down.

what_if.case: Ice cream from today's batch will not sell before closing
what_if.do: In 'Sell it before it goes', press the suggested '{percent}% off' button. The till sells it cheaper until the day ends. Press Stop to end it early.

what_if.case: The plan says 'Not enough history'
what_if.do: It needs 28 days of sales and use. Until then, decide yourself how many to make.

what_if.case: We made the whole plan this morning
what_if.do: Open 'Record the plan in one go', untick what was not made, change what came out where it differs, press 'Record {n} batch(es)', then 'Print {n} label(s)'.

tips: The plan's 'Record these' fills in the form for you; you still check and press Record batch.
Leave 'What came out' empty when it came out as the recipe says.

Sales use the batch with the earliest use-by first, and a batch past its use-by last.

tasks.title: Sign in for the first time
tasks.why: You need your own login before you can use the app. The owner or general manager invites your email first.
before: The owner or general manager added your email on Settings → People and roles.

steps.do: Open the app. You see the sign-in page “Welcome back”.
Press “First time here? Create your login”.
Type the email the owner invited, and a password of at least 8 characters. Press “Create my login”.
steps.see: “Check your email and open the confirmation link. If the owner invited this address, you can then sign in.”

steps.do: Open the email and press the confirmation link.
Come back to the app. Type your email and password and press “Sign in”.
steps.see: The app opens on your first screen: the till for a cashier, Production for a barista, Stock Count for a counter, Purchasing for purchasing, Reports for the accountant and auditor, the Dashboard for managers.

steps.do: Choose your language in the top bar (English, العربية, کوردی). The page reloads in it.
If you want to start on another screen: press your name at the top right (My account) and choose it under “First screen”.
steps.see: “Saved: you start there from now on.”

if.case: It says “Your login is not linked to the business yet”
if.do: You used a different email from the one invited. Ask the owner to add that email on Settings → People and roles, then sign out and sign in again.

if.case: You forgot your password
if.do: On the sign-in page press “Forgot password?”, type your email and press “Send me a reset link”. Open the link in the email.

if.case: No confirmation email came
if.do: Check the spam folder. The email must be exactly the one the owner typed.

tasks.title: Keep your login safe and set your approval PIN
tasks.why: Two-step sign-in stops anyone who learns your password. Managers also need an approval PIN to approve discounts, refunds, voids and losses.
before: An authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator…) for two-step sign-in.

steps.do: Press your name at the top right to open My account.
Under “Two-step sign-in” press “Turn on two-step sign-in”. Scan the code with the authenticator app (or type the key shown).
Type the six digits the app shows in “Then type the six digits it shows” and press “Turn it on”.
steps.see: From now on, after your password, the page “One more step” asks for the six digits.

steps.do: Managers only (owner, general manager, branch manager): under “Your approval PIN” type a PIN in “New PIN” and again in “The same PIN again”. Press “Save the PIN”.
steps.see: “Your PIN is saved.”

steps.do: To change your password: type it in “New password” and “Repeat the new password”, then press “Save password”.
steps.see: “Your password is changed.”

if.case: At the till a manager sees “{name} has not set a PIN yet (My account)”
if.do: That manager opens My account and saves an approval PIN.

if.case: “Approvals by PIN are paused for {name} after too many wrong PINs today”
if.do: That manager sets a new PIN on My account.

if.case: You lost the phone with the authenticator app
if.do: On the sign-in step, press “Lost your phone? Use a backup code” and type one of the eight backup codes you kept when you turned it on. You are let in with the second step off: turn it on again with the new phone (it gives you new codes).

tasks.title: Add the ways the café is paid, and a service charge
tasks.why: Cash and the card machine are always there. Add FIB, FastPay, ZainCash, Qi Card or a bank, so the till offers them and each keeps its own money apart.

steps.do: Open Settings (Menu → Accountant → Settings) and open the group “Selling”.
Under Ways to pay, press “+ FIB”, “+ FastPay”, “+ ZainCash” or “+ Qi Card” for each one the café takes.
steps.see: “{name} added: the till offers it now.”

steps.do: For another app or bank, type its name in “Another, by its name” and press “Add”.
For a service charge: under Service charge, type the percentage in “Service charge on {way} (%)” (for example Dine-in) and press “Save”. Leave other ways empty for none.
Open the till and check the new ways show under the total.

if.case: A way to pay has a wrong name
if.do: Press “Rename”, type the new name and press “Save”. Its account is renamed too.

if.case: The café stops taking one
if.do: Press “Take out of use”. Its money stays in its account; move it on Sales → Ways to Pay.

if.case: The part says “This needs the database update 0069, which has not been applied yet.”
if.do: Ask whoever looks after the system to apply the update.

tasks.title: Set up your own receipt
tasks.why: Every receipt can carry your logo, the café's name in Arabic and Kurdish, a thank-you line, your pages, the Wi-Fi and a QR code.
before: A logo picture (PNG, JPEG or WebP). A dark logo on a light background prints best.

steps.do: Open Settings → Selling → The receipt.
Press “Choose a logo” and pick the picture. It is saved at once.

Fill the boxes you want: “The café's name” (In Arabic, In Kurdish), “Thank-you line” in each language, “Your pages” (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok), “Wi-Fi” (name and password), and “A line at the foot” (address, phone, hours).
Choose where the QR code leads: “No QR code”, “Our menu” or “Tell us how we did”, and paste the link (it starts with https://).
Press “Save the receipt”.
steps.see: “Saved: every receipt prints it from now on.”

steps.do: On the till, press Printing and then “Test print” to see it on paper.

if.case: The logo is too big
if.do: It must be smaller than 60 KB after it is made small. Use a simpler picture.

if.case: You want the café's emblem again
if.do: Press “Take the logo off”.

tasks.title: Add a new person: their login, roles and PIN

steps.do: Owner or general manager: open Settings → People and roles. Under “Add a person” type the Name and Email.
Tick their roles (Cashier is ticked to start with). With more than one place, choose “Works at”. Press “Add person”.
steps.see: “Added. Ask them to create their login with {email}.” They show as “invited”.

steps.do: Ask them to sign in the first time with “First time here? Create your login”, using exactly that email.
Open Staff (Menu → Operations → Staff) and press “Add people”.
Fill a row: Name, What they do, Phone, Where they work, Started on. In “Their login, if they have one” choose their login.
Let them type their own PIN in “PIN (optional)” (4 to 8 digits, not 1111 or 1234). Press “Add to the staff”.
steps.see: “{n} added to the staff.”

steps.do: Check them on the list. Open their line to see their panel.

if.case: A branch manager cannot open Settings
if.do: Only the owner and general manager give logins and roles. A branch manager adds the person on Staff only.

if.case: The Owner or General manager role is greyed: “Only the owner can give this role”
if.do: Only the owner gives those two roles.

if.case: The new cashier still cannot sign in
if.do: Check the Login column: “invited” means they have not created their login yet.

if.case: Two people have the same name
if.do: The screen refuses it. Add a surname or a nickname.

tasks.title: Set a person's pay
tasks.why: Payroll is drafted from each person's pay and their hours. Without pay, the month's payroll cannot be approved.
before: The person is on Staff.

steps.do: Open Staff and press the person's line.
Open the “Pay” tab.
Choose how they are paid: “By the month”, “By the day” or “By the hour”, and type the rate (“Pay a month”, “Pay a day” or “Pay an hour”).
Check “A day's hours” (8 to start) and “Overtime at”. Empty overtime uses the café's rule (150%).
Type “Why it changes (optional)” and press “Save the pay”. The next payroll draft uses it.

if.case: A branch manager cannot see the Pay tab
if.do: Only the owner, general manager and accountant set pay (the Pay tab). The auditor can read a person's pay but not change it.

tasks.title: Add stock items and their opening stock
tasks.why: Every ingredient, cup and bottle is a stock item. Recipes, deliveries, counts and the till all use them.
before: A list of items, ideally in Excel or Google Sheets (name, unit, reorder level, and for the owner what is on the shelf and its cost).

steps.do: Open Inventory (Menu → Operations → Inventory) and press “Add stock item”.
For many items: open “Paste a list”, copy the rows from the spreadsheet and paste them in “The list to add”. Choose “Type for all the rows”.
Fix any row marked red, then press “Add {n} item(s)”.
steps.see: “{n} item(s) added.” Rows not added stay in the box with what to put right.

steps.do: For one item: open “One item”. Type “Name (English)” (and Arabic and Kurdish), choose “Type” and “Measured in”, the pack it is bought in and “Holds”, and the “Reorder level”. Press “Add item”.
Owner only: type what is on the shelf in “Opening stock”, its “Cost per {unit} (IQD)” and “Where the opening stock came from” (for example “the opening count on the first day”).
Owner, for an item added without stock: press “Opening stock”, choose the item, type “Quantity on the shelf”, its unit and cost, and “Where it came from”. Press “Record opening stock”.
steps.see: “Opening stock of {name}: {qty} {unit}, worth {value} (journal {no}).”

if.case: The name looks like an existing item
if.do: If it is the same thing, open the existing one (“Open it”). If it is different, press “It is a different item: add it”.

if.case: Others see “Its stock comes in with a delivery. Opening stock, the owner's capital, is the owner's to record.”
if.do: Only the owner records opening stock. Others add the item; its stock comes with a delivery.

if.case: You chose the wrong base unit
if.do: The base unit never changes later. Take the item out of use on its stock card and add it again correctly.

tasks.title: Add a supplier and what you buy from them
tasks.why: Deliveries, bills and What to buy need the supplier. An item's usual supplier, pack and price let What to buy fill itself in.
before: The stock items exist on Inventory.

steps.do: Open Vendors (Menu → Spending → Vendors) and open the “New vendor” tab.
Type “Vendor name”, “What they supply” and “Phone”. Press “Add vendor”.
steps.see: “Added {name}.”

steps.do: Optional: open “Edit vendor” and type “Days a delivery takes” and “Delivers every (days)”. Press “Save changes”.
Open Inventory and press the item's name to open its stock card.
Under “Bought from” choose the Supplier, the Pack, and type “Price of a pack”. Tick “The usual supplier”. Press “Save the supplier”.
Do the same for each item you buy from them.

if.case: A supplier with the same name exists
if.do: Two suppliers in use cannot share a name. Use the existing one.

if.case: The pack you need is not offered
if.do: On the stock card, under Units, add it: “New unit” (for example case_24), “Label”, “Holds”, then “Add unit”.

if.case: You are on Purchasing
if.do: You can also add a supplier there under “Add supplier” and press “Add”.

tasks.title: Add something you make in batches (gelato, a base, dough)
tasks.why: A batch recipe tells Production what one batch takes from stock and what it makes, so stock and cost stay right.
before: The ingredients exist as stock items.

steps.do: Open Production and scroll to “What you make”. Press “Add something you make”.
Type the “Name”. In “It is” choose “Something new to keep in stock” (or “An item already kept” and choose the Item).
Choose “How it is counted”. If it is kept in pans, type “pan” in “Kept in a container? (optional)” and how much one holds.
Type how much “One batch makes” and its unit, and “How long it keeps” in days or hours.
For each ingredient: type part of its name in “Ingredient {n}”, pick it, then type the Quantity and choose the Unit. Press “+ Add ingredient” for more lines.
Write the steps in “How to make it”. Press “Add it”.
steps.see: “Added “{name}”.” A new tile shows under What you make.

if.case: You make a white base, then flavours
if.do: Add the base first. Then add each flavour and choose the base as an ingredient.

if.case: The recipe changes later
if.do: Open its tile, press “Change…”, change it and press “Save changes”. Batches already recorded keep what they used.

if.case: You stopped making it
if.do: Open it and press “Stop making it”. “Make it again” brings it back.

tasks.title: Add a product to the menu with its recipe and prices
